pages.title: A study space that actually works
pages.note: You don't need a perfect or expensive setup. Check off what you already have, pick one or two things to fix this week, and leave the rest!

items: A home base for deep work (desk or table)
A backup spot (library, study room)
A light-review spot for Anki on tired days
Bed stays for sleep, not lectures
Screen near eye level (a stand or a stack of books)
Second screen if you have one: lecture + notes
A chair you can sit in for a two-hour block
Good light: a desk lamp, plus daylight if you can
Clear surface: only today's stuff out
Phone in another room (or out of reach)
Site blocker on during study blocks
Headphones or earplugs for noise
Roommates know your study hours
Water bottle and a snack
Charger and a long cord
Whiteboard or scratch paper
Today's to-do list, written down
Phone away, blocker on
Pick the one task this block is for
Set a timer for the block, and a break after
Fill your water bottle

sections.h: Make it yours (the optional, fun part!)
items: One thing you love looking at
A note with why you chose medicine
A plant, a photo or a print you like
Five-minute desk reset at your stop time
Set out tomorrow's first task
After two weeks: where did I focus best?

pins.title: Med Student Study Space Setup: A Simple Checklist That Works
